@graph.definition: Borehole drilled into a formation shown to be potentially productive, and is used to obtain more information a resource.
Borehole drilled to obtain samples for laboratory testing and coal analysis.

Borehole drilled into an area or zone already proven to be productive, in order to assist in the recovery of a resource (eg, oil, gas, water). Includes service wells for hydrocarbon recovery, and CSG methane release wells.
Borehole drilled to obtain samples of or from strata for laboratory analysis of parameters which may impact on the environment, including water quality.

A borehole drilled primarily for the purpose of exploration for natural resources. ie, into an unproven area to determine and evaluate the resource potential and production capabilities of a previously undeveloped area or zone.
Borehole drilled for gas analysis. Typical applications include exploration, compliance and greenhouse gas emissions.
A borehole drilled primarily for the purpose of collecting samples for geochemical analysis.
Borehole drilled to investigate the geotechnical properties of the strata and provide samples for mechanical testing.
Borehole drilled to investigate water level, or piezometer installation.
Borehole drilled to obtain samples to determine the amount of oxidation of any coal seam by either visual and tactile or coal analysis methods.
A groundwater borehole used for the purpose of monitoring. (eg, groundwater levels)
A generic term to cover boreholes drilled primarily for the purpose of scientific research.
Borehole drilled under a scientific investigation consent granted under the OPGGS Act 2006 (amended 2012) or of the repealed Petroleum (Submerged Lands) Act 1967.
A borehole drilled for the purpose of underground storage of a commodity (eg, CO2 sequestration, aquifer storage and recovery)
Borehole drilled to provide a conduit or access to and from mine workings for equipment or materials.
A borehole drilled primarily for the purpose of stratigraphic investigation.
Borehole drilled to investigate the attitude of strata and the impact of any tectonic features.
The purpose for drilling the borehole is not known.
A groundwater borehole drilled for the primary purpose of water supply. The bores may supply water for irrigation, stock, domestic use, or industrial use.
